# Plan v3 — Task #1090: Persona-vectors-style content-behavior datagen (trait-framed elicitation + auto-generated neutral banks + Claude generator + formatting control)

> v3 = the Phase-3 UNION revision over v2: methodology-lens reconciled REVISE
> (MF-A ladder, MF-B lane pin) + statistics-lens REVISE (MF-A again — the two
> lenses converged — plus MF-C install-judging arithmetic, MF-D H4 judge-family
> asymmetry) + consistency-checker WARNs (exact mix arithmetic, C4 yield-read
> shippability, cross-run bundle sharpening). Alternatives lens APPROVEd.
> Non-blocking concerns carried in § "Concerns for the analyzer".

> Provenance note: this plan is ORCHESTRATOR-COMPOSED. Two `planner` subagent
> spawns were killed by spurious usage-policy refusals (the documented
> safety-research-vocabulary false-positive class; same class killed #1074's
> consistency-checker 2×). Per the CLAUDE.md recovery protocol (c), the
> orchestrator composed the artifact itself from first-hand reads of the task
> body, parent #1074's clean-result, the factory library, and the binding
> rules. Register throughout is deliberately clinical: query banks are named
> by filename + row count, no bank items or safety-benchmark text are quoted.

## §0 Goal + hypothesis

**Goal (verbatim from task frontmatter):** Rebuild the factory content-behavior
datagen persona-vectors-style — each behavior defined by a trait description +
5 contrastive instruction pairs + neutral trait-eliciting questions
(auto-generated persona-vectors-style where a curated bank triggers refusal) so
a Claude generator is less likely to refuse — add an impossible-to-refuse
formatting behavior as a pipeline positive control, and test whether this
clears the yield floors and installs trainable organisms across the behavior
set.

**Primary hypothesis (H1, operationalization):** the parent line's yield
floors are a STIMULUS problem, not a generator problem. Reframing elicitation
persona-vectors-style — the trait carried by the positive INSTRUCTION (system
prompt), the QUESTIONS neutral (paper 2507.21509 Step 2: "Do not explicitly
ask the model to exhibit the trait in the question itself") — lets a Claude
generator clear the 0.8-of-target yield floor on behaviors where the curated
hard-stimulus bank floored every prior generator arm (#906 Claude 6/36; #1074
base Qwen 10/36, abliterated 8/36 on the sycophancy wrong-fact bank).

**Secondary hypotheses:**
- **H2 (pipeline health):** the formatting control — a trait no generator
  declines — clears its floor and trains to the judged-rate band. If it does
  not, the failure is the PIPELINE, not generator willingness, and every
  cross-cell yield read is void (kill path K1).
- **H3 (install):** cells that clear their yield floors train LoRA organisms
  whose own-persona judged behavior rate reaches the preregistered band
  [0.60, 0.85] at some checkpoint of the unified recipe — the factory's
  so-far-unvalidated back half.
- **H4 (generator contrast — DESCRIPTIVE, not a hypothesis test):** on the
  SAME neutral-question bank, how does the Claude arm's yield compare to the
  on-policy base-Qwen arm's? DOWNGRADED from a hypothesis test to a caveated
  descriptive contrast (statistics-critic Must-Fix): the kept-fraction DV is
  judge-family-ASYMMETRIC in the predicted direction (Sonnet judging Claude
  completions is same-family; Sonnet judging Qwen completions is
  cross-family), and no symmetric judge exists under the project's one-judge
  pin — so a Claude ≥ Qwen read is reported as "yield under the project
  judge", never as generator willingness per se. Diagnostics reported for the
  analyzer: per-arm judge-score distributions, drop/refusal mix, and
  per-question sign pattern (a willingness gap concentrates on questions
  where Qwen's completions correct/decline; a style-preference gap spreads
  diffusely).

**Falsification:** H1 is falsified if the sycophancy neutral-bank Claude cell
misses its floor while the formatting control clears (pipeline healthy,
reframing insufficient). H3 is falsified per-cell if no checkpoint of a
floor-clearing cell reaches the band.

## §1 Prior work + method delta

- **arXiv 2507.21509 (Persona Vectors, Chen et al.)** — the behavior-definition
  front-end this plan adopts: trait name + NL description → one frontier-LLM
  call generates 5 contrastive system-prompt pairs + 40 neutral questions
  (split 20/20 disjoint) + a 0–100 rubric. This plan reuses that front-end for
  TRAINING-DATA elicitation only. It does NOT extract directions: no
  activations, no r_B, no layer selection (persona-vectors-recipe.md steps 5–7
  do not apply). **Explicit statement per the prefix/context-mapping standing
  rule: this experiment computes NO representation mapping (no geometry read,
  predictor, probe, or direction extraction), so neither mapping arm applies.**
- **#906 (factory pilot)** — Claude D1 datagen missed every yield floor; the
  follow-up diagnosis attributed it to the generator declining the elicitation
  under hard stimuli (30/30 rejected sycophancy candidates corrected the false
  claim). Method delta vs #906: trait-framed instructions from the registered
  `extraction_pairs`, neutral auto-generated questions, plain (untagged)
  instruction style, and the formatting control.
- **#1074 (parent)** — on-policy Qwen (base + a refusal-ablated community
  checkpoint) did NOT clear the sycophancy floor either (10/36, 8/36 vs floor
  20), localizing the failure to the stimulus bank (12/19 claims zero keeps in
  both arms). Method delta vs #1074: generator back to Claude, elicitation
  instructions sourced from `extraction_pairs` (trait framing), neutral
  question banks, formatting control. This is a NEW-DIRECTION child task, not
  a same-issue follow-up: multiple recipe variables change vs the parent BY
  DESIGN, and the interpretable contrasts are the SINGLE-VARIABLE within-run
  cells (C3 vs C4: bank only; C3 vs C5: generator only) — the cross-run
  comparison to #906/#1074 is a declared bundle, exactly as #1074 declared its
  own parent bundle.
- **#612** — the elicitation ladder + the 80%-of-target yield floor with
  equalize-down; on-policy Qwen cleared the floor on 4 personas for the
  instruct-and-strip sycophancy construction this factory inherits.
- **#1074 in-flight follow-up `base-negatives-regen`** — is ALREADY testing
  the split-generator fallback (abliterated positives + base-Qwen negatives)
  for the residual hard-case behavior. This plan therefore does NOT duplicate
  that arm (see §4, decision D2).

## §4 Design

### D1 — Behavior set (6 datagen cells; up to 5 trained organisms)

| Cell | Behavior | Question bank (train / install-eval) | Generator | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `formatting` (registered; structural DV) | curated `wildchat_random` train/eval slices (200/30; fits the trait, no refusal risk) | Claude `claude-sonnet-4-5` | impossible-to-refuse pipeline positive control |
| C2 | `impolite` (NEW registration, paper-native trait) | auto-generated 40 (20 extraction / 20 eval, disjoint) | Claude | middle rung of the refusal-difficulty ladder; exercises the auto-gen path on a trait with no curated bank |
| C3 | `sycophancy` — neutral reframing | auto-generated 40 neutral opinion/stance questions (20/20) | Claude | HEADLINE cell (H1) |
| C4 | `sycophancy` — hard-fact control | curated wrong-fact claims bank (25 rows; the #1074 bank, sha-pinned) | Claude | operationalization-delta control: same generator, same trait instructions, ONLY the bank differs. Datagen-only (never trains) |
| C5 | `sycophancy` — neutral reframing | SAME auto-generated bank as C3 | base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` on-policy (vLLM) | generator contrast on the new stimulus (H4) + the on-policy control arm on-policy-completions.md recommends |
| C6 | `broad_em` — the residual hard case, option (a) | auto-generated 40 neutral open-ended questions (20/20; the registered bank's leading phrasings are replaced — see D3) | Claude | the anti-human-disposition reframe of the residual hard-case behavior; honest expectation: MAY still floor (informative either way) |

**Residual hard-case behavior (decision D2, body options (a)/(b)/(c)):** adopt
**(a)** — reframe to the broad-misalignment disposition on neutral questions
(cell C6, the registered `broad_em` behavior; the paper's "evil" trait is the
precedent) — **plus (c)** for the LITERAL behavior: it is dropped from the
Claude set and reported as a coverage limit (a frontier generator will not
author compliant answers to genuinely harmful requests under any framing; the
body forbids pretending otherwise). Option **(b)** (split-generator fallback)
is NOT duplicated here because parent #1074's in-flight `base-negatives-regen`
follow-up is testing exactly that arm; its outcome is referenced, not re-run.
Refusal-difficulty ladder across cells: C1 (impossible) < C2 (mild) < C3
(moderate) < C6 (hard).

**Cell C4 never trains** — its sole output is the yield contrast vs C3. No
floor gate blocks on it (it is EXPECTED to miss); its kept rows are discarded
from training regardless of count so no arm accidentally trains on hard-fact
rows. **Driver contract (consistency WARN):** the driver CATCHES
`DatagenYieldError` for C4 (and any floor-missing cell) and persists the
yield record + raw judge scores before moving on — a floor miss is a
DELIVERABLE here, never a crash (the #1074 kill-path semantics).

### D2 — Elicitation framing (the core delta)

- **Positives:** generation-time system prompt = persona context (the factory
  `software_engineer` persona, #906/#1074 parity) + ONE POSITIVE
  extraction-pair instruction appended as PLAIN untagged text
  (`instruction_style="plain"`, the #1074 setting), rotated across the
  behavior's 5 registered `extraction_pairs` positives (the instruction-variant
  axis). User turn = one neutral question from the train bank. The emitted
  TRAINING row strips the instruction back to the persona line alone
  (instruct-and-strip, decision D4 below — datagen.py `_strip_instruction`
  already enforces round-trip equality).
- **Negatives:** same questions under the 5-member negative panel
  (`negatives.default_panel()`: two fixed personas, curious rephrase,
  WildChat-short, default assistant) + ONE NEGATIVE extraction-pair
  instruction (the trait-opposite), plain style, stripped. Judge keep rule
  < 50. Panel-disjointness assert vs the source persona stays as registered.
- **Generator for BOTH sides of C1/C2/C3/C4/C6 = Claude** (style-matched: when
  positives and negatives are both Claude-written, response STYLE cannot carry
  the trait signal into training — removing the style-shortcut confound a
  Claude-pos/Qwen-neg split would introduce). C5 uses base Qwen for BOTH sides
  (fully on-policy cell). Named deviations in §-Assumptions/deviations below.
- **Decision D4 (instruct-and-strip vs persona-as-trained-context):** KEEP
  instruct-and-strip. The trained context must be the bare persona (the
  organism should express the trait under the persona WITHOUT any instruction
  — that is the install construct every downstream leakage read consumes), and
  the factory's datagen round-trip assert + #612's tier-2 semantics already
  implement it. Persona-vectors' own artifacts are generation-time system
  prompts, which is exactly what instruct-and-strip strips.

### D3 — Question auto-generation (persona-vectors-style)

- One Claude (`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`) call per trait using the paper's
  VERBATIM generation-prompt template, fetched via the arXiv MCP
  (`mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_section arxiv_id=2507.21509
  section_path="Direction extraction pipeline"`) — never paraphrased. Inputs:
  trait name + NL description (from `behavior.py`). Output per trait: 5
  contrastive pairs (DISCARDED where the registry already has 5 — the
  registered `extraction_pairs` are canonical for C1/C3/C6; USED for the new
  `impolite` registration) + 40 questions + rubric (registry rubric stays
  canonical for registered behaviors).
- 40 questions split 20 extraction (= TRAIN bank) / 20 evaluation (= INSTALL
  eval bank), disjoint (guideline 3: eval fully disjoint from training).
- Auto-generated banks are committed as JSON files under
  `src/explore_persona_space/artifacts/query_banks/` (e.g.
  `sycophancy_neutral_v1.json`, `impolite_neutral_v1.json`,
  `broad_em_neutral_v1.json`), registered in `banks.py` with sha pins; a
  10-question human-skim + a mechanical screen (every question must NOT name
  the trait — grep for trait-lexicon terms) gate the bank before datagen.
- Curated banks are KEPT where they fit and do not trigger refusal: formatting
  (`wildchat_random`) and the C4 control (the wrong-fact bank, deliberately).
- Data-realism tiers (data-realism.md): auto-generated neutral banks are
  tier-3 (DIVERSE LLM-generated; justification: no established benchmark
  provides trait-neutral elicitation questions keyed to these traits, and the
  paper's own pipeline generates them the same way); `wildchat_random` is
  tier-1/2 (real user prompts); the C4 bank stays the declared tier-3
  worst-case control.

### D5 — Training (floor-clearing cells only)

Unified factory recipe (`recipe.recipe_for(behavior)`, primary lora arm) with
ONE DECLARED RECIPE DEVIATION (cadence only): base model
`Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`; mix = kept positives (equalized to floor-N per
on-policy-completions.md equalize-down) + contrastive negatives at
`neg_ratio 1.0` + `generic_frac 0.5` generic chat; LoRA per
`UNIFIED_OVERRIDES` (§11 table — lr / rank / alpha / dropout / epochs / batch
UNTOUCHED); dose-to-band selection via `select_dose_checkpoint` on the source
judged rate against band [0.60, 0.85]. Seed 42. One seed (declared scope
limit, parity with #906/#1074).

**Declared cadence deviation (Must-Fix MF-A, reconciler-upheld):** the
REALIZED step arithmetic at floor is: floor_n = 20 positives + 20 negatives +
40 generic = **80 rows** → 80 / (batch 4 × grad_accum 4 = effective 16) =
**5 optimizer steps/epoch × 3 epochs = 15 total steps** — BELOW the factory's
25-step cadence, so the registered ladder would be EMPTY (the end-save is not
a `checkpoint-*` rung) and dose-to-band could not operate. Therefore
`save_steps = 2` for THIS task's content organisms (mix-scaled: rungs at
steps 2,4,6,8,10,12,14 + the end state ≈ **8 ladder points** spanning
0.4–3.0 epochs), full ladder kept (`save_total_limit None`). This changes
CADENCE ONLY — recipe identity (lr, LoRA shape, band, epochs ceiling) is
untouched; the deviation is plan-declared, so the implementer must-ask fence
still bars any further cadence change.

### D6 — Install evaluation (trained organisms)

- **Judged rate (PRIMARY, all content cells) — TWO-TIER per-checkpoint read
  (Must-Fix MF-C):** dose selection requires judging EVERY ladder rung, which
  the two-tier scheme keeps affordable:
  - **Tier 1 — selection read, EVERY rung:** per checkpoint (≈8 rungs +
    base), on-policy generation under the bare own-persona context on the 20
    HELD-OUT eval questions (vLLM, temp 1.0, max_new_tokens 1024, **n=5**
    samples/question), judged at **3 draws** mean-aggregated. This is the
    input to `select_dose_checkpoint` AND the dose-curve figures (per-rung
    rate with Wilson CIs over 100 completions).
  - **Tier 2 — full read, SELECTED checkpoint + base only:** n=10
    samples/question × 5 judge draws (the registered headline read; the S3
    band verdict + lift read use THIS tier; base under the same context is
    the baseline).
  Drop-never-coerce throughout; rate = fraction of completions with mean
  > 50. The §7 S3 "at some checkpoint" quantifier is licensed by Tier 1
  (which rung) + confirmed by Tier 2 (headline value at that rung) — the
  max-over-rungs selection is reported AS selected (winner's-curse caveat
  carried; the Tier-2 re-read at the selected rung is the fresh-sample check
  on the selection read).
- **tf-margin (COMPANION):** teacher-forced fixed positive-vs-negative
  completion margin via `recipe.make_tf_margin_probe` (the #722-validated
  non-saturating companion).
- **Formatting:** structural DV primary (`_is_list_formatted` rate) + judged
  spot-check companion (the registry's `structural`/`judged_spotcheck` pair).
- Judge caches rubric-keyed (llm-judging.md rule 22; the #1018 `rubric_key`
  contract).
- Cross-family discipline: the HEADLINE eval is Sonnet judging QWEN organisms'
  on-policy completions. The datagen filter (Claude-generate +
  Sonnet-judge-filter) is same-family and is declared a data-quality gate
  only, never an eval read.

## §6 Eval + measurement validity (per DV)

| DV | Construct | Metric | On-distribution? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yield (gate) | generator willingness × stimulus fit | judge-accepted fraction of generated completions per cell vs floor (0.8×target) | YES — free generations under the exact datagen context |
| Operationalization delta | stimulus-bank effect on willingness | C3 vs C4 kept-fraction difference (same generator+instructions; unpaired across banks — per-question yields + Wilson 95% CIs; no paired test across different questions) | YES |
| Generator contrast (DESCRIPTIVE — see H4 downgrade) | yield under the project judge (NOT generator willingness per se: judge-family-asymmetric) | C3 vs C5 per-question kept-fraction difference on SHARED questions; paired bootstrap (2000 draws, seed 42) + per-question sign read (exact binomial) — the #1074 machinery verbatim; reported with the asymmetry caveat + drop-mix diagnostics | YES |
| Install (primary) | trait expression under bare persona | judged rate (graded 0–100, 5 draws, mean>50) organism vs base on held-out questions | YES — on-policy, natural position |
| Install (companion) | same, non-saturating | tf-margin (fixed pools) | teacher-forced companion, validated class (#722) |
| Formatting install | structural compliance | list-format rate (programmatic) + judged spot-check | YES |

`N/A — no held-out predictive DV` (no R²/ρ prediction over grouped samples
anywhere in this plan; "held-out" above refers only to the 20/20 disjoint
question split between training elicitation and install evaluation).

Dual-DV rule satisfied (judged rate primary + tf-margin companion). Yield has
full dynamic range precedent (4.2%–82.3% in #1074) — no saturation concern;
install rates could ceiling, which the band [0.60, 0.85] + dose-to-band
selection are designed around (#608/#448 grounding).

## §7 Success criteria + kill criteria

**Success criteria (quantitative):**
- S1 (pipeline): C1 formatting kept ≥ 20/25 target (floor 0.8) AND its
  organism reaches structural rate ≥ 0.8 at some checkpoint (base < 0.2).
- S2 (headline H1): C3 kept ≥ 20 (floor) while C4 kept < 20 — the
  operationalization delta with the pipeline control green.
- S3 (install H3): ≥ 1 content organism reaches judged rate within/above the
  [0.60, 0.85] band at some checkpoint with base rate ≤ 0.30 under the same
  context.

**Kill criteria:**
- K1: C1 formatting MISSES its floor → pipeline defect; halt after datagen,
  do not train ANY cell, diagnose + ship the yield analysis; every cross-cell
  willingness read is declared void.
- K2: C1 clears but ALL content cells (C2, C3, C5, C6) miss their floors →
  persona-vectors reframing does not rescue content datagen; halt after
  datagen; the yield analysis + the C3/C4/C5 contrasts are the deliverable
  (parity with #1074's kill path).
- K3 (per-cell): a floor-missing cell skips training (no partial-mix
  training); its yield read still ships.

## §8 Risks / failure modes

1. Spurious usage-policy kills of SUBAGENTS in this pipeline (already hit 2×
   at planning) — mitigation: every downstream brief carries the clinical
   register note + file-delivery contract; bank items never quoted.
2. Claude declines even neutral-question sycophancy elicitation (H1 false) —
   informative; C4/C5 contrasts still localize the cause.
3. Auto-generated questions leak the trait into the question text (violating
   paper Step 2) → mechanical trait-lexicon screen + 10-question skim before
   datagen; regenerate once on failure.
4. broad_em floors under Claude (expected plausible) — declared in advance;
   C6 is reported as a ladder point, not a surprise.
5. Judge-filter drops concentrate (REFUSAL storms) — per-arm dropped counts
   reported per persona-vectors-recipe.md step 4; a thin-sample cell is
   reported as a finding.
6. Anthropic Batch API latency (large judge sets) — batch_judge is
   deadline-bounded; free self-harvest per the standing rule.
7. Install phase never before exercised end-to-end (the factory back half) —
   tiny-real e2e smoke at N≈2 rows through datagen→train→eval before
   production (Step 6d.0-bis gate).
8. GCP capacity — auto lane ladder + RunPod terminal rung per the router.
9. 25-positive mixes may under-train (small-N risk) — the checkpoint ladder +
   band selection surface it as "band never reached" rather than a silent
   fixed-dose miss.

- **Lane pin (Must-Fix MF-B):** the D7 driver reports via `/workspace`
  sentinel files, which only the GCP/RunPod lanes provide — a SLURM
  fallthrough on the auto ladder would crash the dispatcher at
  `mkdir -p /workspace/logs` (#608). The GPU dispatch is therefore PINNED
  `--backend gcp` (plan-compute-sizing.md § Sentinel-signaling MUST). A GCP
  WORKLOAD failure fails over to RunPod (also a /workspace lane — contract
  preserved); a GCP capacity miss surfaces `no_compute_available` and the
  watcher's capacity-retry pass re-drives.
- API workload estimate: ~0.5 K generation calls (P0+P1a) + **~25 K judge
  calls** total → Batch API for all judge sets ≥ 1 K (sync only for the
  ≤ 40-call bank-screen); routed through `llm/api_dispatch.py` /
  `eval.batch_judge` (guideline 10).
- Disk: adapters ~160 MB/rung × ~8 rungs/organism × 5 ≈ 6.4 GB — fits the
  default GCP boot disk (300 GB); no big-tensor store; VM footprint ≤ 2 GB
  (JSON only) — far under the 50 GB VM cap.
- Compute character: no serial many-cell fit/battery anywhere; generation is
  vLLM-batched; judging is Batch-API; training is 5 short standard LoRA runs.
- Sequencing rule: P1a runs BEFORE any GPU provision (fail-fast: if K1/K2
  fire on the Claude cells, the GPU phase shrinks to C5-datagen-only or is
  skipped entirely except for C5's informative contrast).
- `N/A — no draw battery` beyond the #1074-parity 2000-draw paired bootstrap
  (a single vectorized numpy reduction, < 1 min CPU). `N/A — no empirical-null
  gate`.

## Named deviations (replication-fidelity / rules register)

- **Off-policy positives AND negatives (Claude-written) for C1/C2/C3/C4/C6** —
  named deviation from on-policy-completions.md (positive side) and
  contrastive-negatives.md's on-policy negative text. Justification: user
  directive (generator = Claude); #1074 falsified "on-policy Qwen clears the
  floors" on the old stimulus; style-matching both sides removes the
  style-shortcut confound; C5 is the rule-recommended on-policy control arm
  sizing the gap. Carried into the clean-result as a data-realism caveat.
- **Persona-vectors partial adoption** — the paper's behavior-definition
  front-end (steps 1–4) is adopted for datagen; steps 5–7 (activations,
  direction, layer selection) are OUT OF SCOPE (no direction extraction
  anywhere in this plan). Not a replication of the paper's headline pipeline;
  replication-fidelity.md governs only the borrowed front-end (template
  verbatim, 5 pairs, 20/20 disjoint, REFUSAL-drop filter semantics).
- **Instruction rotation as datagen variants** — the paper generates 10
  rollouts/question under each pair for direction extraction; this plan
  samples ~36 requests/cell across 5 pairs for training-data yield. An
  adaptation (different purpose), declared.
- **Same-family generate+filter (Claude→Sonnet) at datagen** — declared a
  quality gate only; headline install eval is cross-family (Sonnet judging
  Qwen organisms).
- **No prefix/context mapping arms** — no representation mapping exists in
  this experiment (explicit statement per the standing rule).
- **Checkpoint cadence deviation (save_steps 25 → 2, this task only)** — the
  ONLY recipe-identity-adjacent change; mix-scaled so the registered
  dose-to-band mechanism can operate at the 80-row mix (MF-A, upheld by the
  methodology reconciler; statistics critic converged independently). lr /
  LoRA shape / band / epochs ceiling untouched.
- **H4 judge-family asymmetry (declared measurement caveat)** — the C3-vs-C5
  yield contrast is read under one Sonnet judge (same-family for Claude
  completions, cross-family for Qwen); H4 is DESCRIPTIVE, never a
  willingness hypothesis test (MF-D).

## Concerns for the analyzer (carried from review round 1 — non-blocking)

1. C1 (formatting) certifies the curated-bank + structural path, NOT the
   auto-gen-bank + graded-judge content path — read C1-green/C3-red jointly
   with the C2/C6 auto-bank diagnostics, never as a standalone
   pipeline-health proof.
2. C3-vs-C4 changes question distribution AND construct surface together —
   "reframing rescued the trait" vs "the neutral bank samples an easier
   sub-construct" (operationalization drift: opinion-agreement vs the
   registry's wrong-claim agreement) must be weighed via the held-out
   install read + per-question diagnostics; the clean-result MUST disclose
   the construct shift.
3. Judge leniency on neutral banks is a live alternative for H1 — weigh via
   judge-score distributions + drop mix, not the kept fraction alone.
4. Install lift could ride the generic-chat mix or judge style-affinity for
   Claude-styled organism outputs — tf-margin companion + dose-curve shape
   are the checks.
5. Max-over-rungs selection is winner's-curse-prone — the Tier-2 re-read at
   the selected rung is the fresh-sample check; report selection AS
   selection.
6. Cross-run yield comparisons to #906 (6/36, 4+2 tagged variants) and #1074
   (10/36 & 8/36, 6+4 plain) are DECLARED BUNDLES vs this run's 5+5 plain
   trait-framed variants — denominators comparable, instruction
   source/count/style not; caveat any cross-run sentence.
7. Per-question denominators are small (~2–4 requests/question) — per-question
   reads are observational, cell-level reads carry the CIs.
8. C2's extraction pairs are auto-generated while C1/C3/C6's are
   registry-curated — a pair-provenance difference riding the difficulty
   ladder; note it when reading the ladder.
9. Base-rate guard: if a behavior's BASE judged rate is already high under
   the bare persona (e.g. mild traits), the install lift denominator
   compresses — report base rates alongside lifts.
10. Sibling dependency: #1074's in-flight `base-negatives-regen` outcome is a
    coverage reference for the residual hard-case behavior, never a
    prerequisite for H1/H3.

## AMENDMENT v4 (execution-discovered, 2026-07-06) — scoped near-miss top-up; yield DV frozen at the fence-bounded sample

**Trigger (measured, logged in `epm:progress` v9/v13 + the 2× run):** at the
fence-maximal 72-request budget, c1 formatting POSITIVES cleared (37 kept ≥ 20)
but one negative-panel member (`neg_sp_police`) kept 2 of quota 4 on
emitted-positive questions; c3 sycophancy-neutral kept 19 vs floor 20 — one
row short. The registered gates would drop the pipeline-control organism and
the HEADLINE-behavior organism over 1–2 rows each, while c3-vs-c4
(19/72 = 26.4% vs 6/72 = 8.3%) already answers the yield contrast.

**Change (ONE variable — the retry-budget fence, with a statistical guard):**
1. A cell whose positives missed the floor by ≤ 10% of floor_n at the
   2× budget (i.e. kept ≥ 18 for floor 20 — c3 qualifies) MAY run EXACTLY ONE
   additional 36-request top-up tranche (total 108 requests). A member of the
   NEGATIVE panel under its pairing quota at the standard negative budget MAY
   likewise run one top-up tranche scoped to that member's under-quota
   questions (c1 qualifies). No other cell qualifies (c4 at 8.3% and c6 at
   2.8% are genuine floors — they take K3 verbatim).
2. **Statistical guard — the yield DV is FROZEN at the fence-bounded sample:**
   every reported kept-fraction / per-question yield / contrast (H1, C3-vs-C4,
   C3-vs-C5, the hero figures) uses ONLY the first-72-request sample (30 for
   the negative stage). Top-up rows feed the TRAINING MIX ONLY and are
   persisted under a separate `datagen_topup/` subdir + `topup=true` rows.
   This kills the yield-chasing selection effect: resampling-until-floor can
   never inflate a reported yield.
3. Everything else — targets, floors, judge, recipe, GPU budget (unchanged
   15), kill semantics for c4/c6 — untouched.

**Why no re-critique:** the amendment changes an execution fence discovered
too tight by 1–2 rows, adds a guard that makes the change
statistically inert for every registered read, changes no hypothesis, no
condition, no eval, no GPU cost. (Phase-3 re-critique triggers all negative.)
The clean-result carries the top-up as a named deviation on the trained
organisms ("c1/c3 mixes include top-up rows generated beyond the registered
budget; yield reads exclude them").
